newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan's EVA, Formosa to open China offices soon.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's EVA, Formosa to open China offices soon.

text.p: Taiwan's EVA Airways and Formosa Airlines are planning to open offices in China, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The newspaper, published by the official China Daily, said the airlines would open offices in response to a rise in civil aviation exchanges and the possibility of future direct air links between the two political rivals.
Taipei has banned all direct links with the mainland since a civil war separated the two sides in 1949. All flights must be routed through a third territory, usually Hong Kong.
China has agreed to maintain Hong Kong as a stopover for flights from its island rival after Beijing resumes control over the territory on July 1, 1997.
Taiwan's China Airlines set up a representative office in Beijing in June to handle customer service and sales.
China Airlines has signed check-in agreements with several mainland carriers to allow its passengers to change planes in Hong Kong without having to check in again.
